findings.finding: The leaf priority-consumer census is VERIFIED and complete, but the plan separately names _map_local_to_jira_fields, _map_local_to_dc_fields, and map_fields_to_remote as symbols gaining a new priority_map param while leaving the threading/caller inventory as a single un-enumerated Scope line ('MODIFY call sites that construct create/update payloads to pass the effective maps'). The concrete resolve-and-thread sites that carry status_map today — and by the plan's own S2 analogy must carry priority_map — are not named: outbound_mutation_builders._build_create/update (resolves _effective_status_map_for at :80 and :235 and passes status_map into map_local_to_remote), the seam wrappers map_local_to_remote/map_fields_to_remote in adapters/jira/backend.py and adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py, and the intermediate hop compute_update_fields in outbound_field_diff.py that threads status_map down to map_fields_to_remote.
findings.location: Scope: 'MODIFY call sites that construct create/update payloads to pass the effective maps (resolved once per project per pass).'
scenarios: outbound_mutation_builders.py create leg (line 80/87): if not modified to resolve effective_priority_map and pass priority_map into map_local_to_remote, CREATE payloads keep using the built-in and the projects.KEY.priority_map overlay never takes effect on create — silently under-delivering AC test_priority_config_effect.

compute_update_fields (outbound_field_diff.py:235) + outbound_mutation_builders.py:235 update leg: if the priority_map is not threaded through this hop to map_fields_to_remote, UPDATE payloads ignore the overlay, so the update consumer at outbound_mapper.py:144 is unreachable from config despite being in the census.

Seam wrappers map_local_to_remote/map_fields_to_remote in jira/backend.py and jira_datacenter/backend.py: if their signatures do not gain priority_map, the resolved map cannot cross the backend boundary to the leaf functions, breaking the DC create consumer at backend.py:87.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the S4/S5 boundary with the parent: either (a) narrow S5 (a881) to create_defaults-only and leave the priority axis to S4, or (b) update the parent epic 3d7a's child decomposition to record that the priority axis moved into S5 (and rescope S4 to link relations only), so 'responsibilities do not overlap' still holds.
evidence: Parent 3d7a decomposition: 'S4 — Link-relation + priority mapping via the seam retires RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK/UNSYNCED_RELATIONS/LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA to the seam.'
Parent 3d7a decomposition: 'S5 — create_defaults injection on create prevents required-custom-field create failures.'
Parent 3d7a: '(each criterion maps to ≥1 child; responsibilities do not overlap)'

Leaf a881 title and Approach: 'S5 does the same for TWO axes … 1. PRIORITY … Make it config-driven … 2. create_defaults'; ACs include test_priority_config_effect / test_priority_drifts covering the priority axis the parent assigned to S4.

The work stays inside the epic's overall contract (epic AC#3 covers the priority axis; AC#7 covers create_defaults), so this is a partition/enumeration mismatch, not an escape from the parent contract.
findings.finding: Leaf S5 (a881) delivers the config-driven PRIORITY mapping that the parent epic's child decomposition explicitly assigns to sibling S4 ('S4 — Link-relation + priority mapping via the seam … retires … LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA to the seam'), while the parent scopes S5 as 'create_defaults injection on create' and states 'responsibilities do not overlap.' The leaf thus re-draws the parent's internal S4/S5 boundary, risking overlap or a coverage gap with the S4 ticket.
findings.location: S5 (a881) — whole plan (title 'Config-driven priority mapping + per-project create_defaults'; Scope/AC items test_priority_config_effect, test_priority_drifts); parent 3d7a 'Child decomposition' (S4 vs S5 lines + 'responsibilities do not overlap')
scenarios: If a separate S4 ticket still carries the priority axis, both tickets edit the same consumers (outbound_mapper.py resolve_outbound_priority, outbound_fields.py, jira_datacenter/backend.py, config.py) — duplicated/conflicting edits.

If S4 was silently assumed to no longer own priority, the S4 ticket may ship only link relations and leave priority double-counted here without the parent decomposition being updated to reflect the move.
